## Parts without a verified spaceflight fact (shown as "Gap" in the app)

- ribs: No site-specific spaceflight figure collected for the ribs; the whole-body skeleton figures apply.
- shoulder: No site-specific spaceflight figure collected for the shoulder girdle.
- arm: No site-specific spaceflight figure collected for the arm bones.
- hand: No site-specific spaceflight figure collected for the hand bones.
- shin: No site-specific figure collected for the lower leg.
- foot: No site-specific spaceflight figure collected for the foot bones.
- airway: No airway measurement is connected; dust exposure matters mainly on the Moon.
- liver: Animal evidence only; no verified human measurement or threshold collected.
- stomach: Little verified data; energy intake is tracked through nutrition assessment.
- intestine: Constipation is common; no verified threshold collected.
- brain: No verified countermeasure list collected for sleep in this work.
- eye: No verified countermeasure collected; report vision changes to the flight surgeon.
- tendon: No verified spaceflight data collected for tendons.

## How to read a rule's basis

- verified: the number or statement is in the cited source.
- reference: compared with a verified NASA reference value (for example mean bone loss per month); the cut-offs around it are a convention.
- convention: general clinical convention (for example WHO anemia cut-off, resting heart-rate limits, 80 % of the radiation limit). Not NASA-specific and not verified here.
- model: model output, not a measurement.

Known weak points: spleen to anemia link and part descriptions (`does`) are textbook statements; the liver and gut evidence is animal or press-based; urine volume and calcium cut-offs, back-pain cut-offs and the sleep-hours cut-offs are conventions.
